text:
NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions and residual connections provide natural intervention sites: residual branches, block outputs and temporal positions grouped by receptive field ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163)). Activation-patching research warns that corruption choice and evaluation metric can substantially change localization results; compare clean-to-corrupted restoration with corrupted-to-clean disruption, using continuous target–distractor score margins alongside ranking outcomes ([ICLR 2024](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/06a52a54c8ee03cd86771136bc91eb1f-Abstract-Conference.html), [practical guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255)). ICLR 2025’s ORION retrieval experiments demonstrate structured counterfactual tasks and residual-stream patching that separate request processing from context retrieval. This supports the experimental approach, but does not establish equivalent mechanisms in NextItNet ([paper](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/ad36c2cfc423e75c6d68d751a955b22e-Paper-Conference.pdf)).

Proposed adaptation, rather than an established NextItNet diagnostic: construct controlled history pairs preserving a recent motif while varying older distractors; separately vary motif order and distance across dilation receptive fields. Test padding invariance by adding leading zeros without truncating history and reading the final nonpadding position. Patch individual residual branches and relevant temporal spans within the same trained category model. Calibrate localization against temporary known faults—disabled branches, altered dilation or incorrect padding/readout—and identity patches plus mathematically equivalent padding as negative controls. Report fault-detection rate, false alarms, injected-block localization accuracy and score-margin restoration; avoid normalized restoration when the clean–corrupted gap is near zero. Synthetic temporal tasks require demonstrated baseline competence before failure interpretation. These probes require neither auxiliary fitted predictors nor score fusion; benchmark selection remains the fixed macro validation HR@10.
